 Grand Forks City Council Approves Deadline Extension For Special Assessment Deferral Process For New Residential Construction, Also Approves Tax Incentive For Cirrus Aircraft
 By Alex Carmenaty 
 Nov 17, 2026 | 7:35 AM 
 (KNOX) – The Grand Forks City Council approved to extend the deadline to 2029 for the special assessment deferral process for new residential construction. 
 This three year deferral program is so any special assessments that are levied against residential greenfield developments (single family and townhomes) are deferred for three years. This gives developers or homeowners extra time to avoid payments. 
 City Administrator Todd Feland. 
 https://media-cdn.socastsrm.com/wordpress/wp-content/blogs.dir/2404/files/2026/11/feland.wav 
 The deferral program has been in action since 2020 and the new deadline for deferrals is October 31st, 2029. 
 The vote to extend the deadline was passed after a public hearing was held. No members of the public spoke during the hearing. 
 Meanwhile, the Grand Forks City Council also approved a five year, 100 percent expanding business property tax incentive for Cirrus Aircraft. Cirrus is planning to start with the second phase of the project which includes a 50,000 square foot expansion and 13 new staff members. The vote passed 5-1, with Councilwoman Rebecca Osowski voting against. Osowski says she doesn’t want to give Cirrus tax breaks because of its relationship and ties with China, but also explains there’s more to her vote. 
 https://media-cdn.socastsrm.com/wordpress/wp-content/blogs.dir/2404/files/2026/11/rebecca-1-1.wav 
 Last year, the council approved a 10 year, 100 percent tax incentive for an earlier expansion.
